## 2. Enterprise B2B Service Level Agreement (SLA) Specifications

### Comprehensive vs. Non-Comprehensive Printer AMCs

| Dimension | Comprehensive Printer AMC | Non-Comprehensive (Labour-Only) AMC |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Labour & Breakdown Visits** | 100% Unlimited Included (Emergency & Preventive) | Included (Routine visits covered) |
| **Electronic Components** | Main Logic Boards, Power Supply Boards, Sensor Arrays covered at ₹0 | Billed separately per incident at market prices |
| **Mechanical Wear Parts** | Fuser Assemblies, Pressure Rollers, Nylon Tractor Gears, Pickup Rollers covered | Billed separately per component |
| **Printhead & Needles** | Re-pinning covered or subsidised per contract tier | Excluded; billed per replacement |
| **On-Site Response SLA** | **Guaranteed 4-Hour On-Site Arrival** across MMR | Next business day (24 to 48 hours) |
| **Standby Buffer Units** | **Guaranteed Identical Hot-Swap Machine** if repair exceeds SLA | Subject to vendor inventory availability |
| **Budget Predictability** | 100% Fixed Annual Operational Expenditure (OPEX) | Variable quarterly expenditure with unexpected repair spikes |
| **Average Cost Reduction** | Up to 40% lower Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) | High administrative overhead from quote approvals |

### The 4-Hour Breakdown Response Protocol
* For enterprise clients operating mission-critical printers (bank teller desks, logistics loading docks, pathology labs), Rex International guarantees a 4-hour on-site arrival SLA dispatched from the central Mulund West facility.
* If component-level diagnosis indicates that on-site micro-soldering or ultrasonic cleaning is required, a pre-calibrated standby printer from our buffer inventory is installed immediately to maintain continuous business uptime.

### Scheduled Preventive Maintenance (PM) Protocols
Over 70% of electromechanical printer failures are caused by environmental paper lint, abrasive dust, and toner particulate. Rex International preventive contracts mandate:
1. **Pneumatic Micro-Cleansing:** High-velocity dry air purging to clean optical feed phototransistors, registration sensors, and carriage guide rails.
2. **Fuser Film Re-greasing:** Application of 300°C high-temperature synthetic fluorinated grease to eliminate Teflon sleeve tearing and accordion paper jams.
3. **Platen Gap Calibration:** Re-zeroing the needle-to-platen distance on dotmatrix impact units to prevent needle bending across multi-part continuous forms.
4. **Stepper Current Diagnostics:** Testing motor coil resistance to detect mechanical gear binding before driver ICs overheat.

## 3. Engineering Protocols & Component-Level Diagnostics

### A. Dotmatrix Impact Technology (24-Pin & 9-Pin)
* **Mechanics:** Tungsten-alloy wire needles driven by electromagnetic solenoids strike inked nylon ribbon against paper backed by a rubber platen roller.
* **Failure Mode: Tractor Gear Stripping:**
  * *Root Cause:* High-volume 4-part continuous stationery placed too far below printer or clamped with excessive lateral margin tension. High-torque metal stepper pinion strips softer factory nylon reduction gears.
  * *Remediation:* Installation of industrial Delrin (polyacetal) composite gears, drive shaft truing, and dry PTFE lubrication that does not attract airborne paper lint.
* **Failure Mode: Printhead Needle Snapping:**
  * *Root Cause:* Operating with platen gap lever set to "1" (single-sheet) while feeding 3-part or 4-part carbonized forms. Needles bend or snap off at the ruby jewel guide.
  * *Remediation:* Component-level 24-pin tungsten wire replacement, jewel guide alignment, and coil resistance testing at under 50% of OEM module replacement cost.

### B. Epson Micro Piezo™ Ink Tank Technology
* **Mechanics:** Microscopic piezoelectric ceramic elements physically flex when subjected to an electric charge, ejecting ink droplets through 20-to-30-micron nozzle apertures without thermal stress.
* **Failure Mode: Persistent Horizontal White Streaks:**
  * *Root Cause:* Ambient heat evaporates volatile glycols in idle printheads, forming hardened pigment resin crusts across the nozzle face. Repeated automated driver cleanings introduce air cavitation into dampers and fill waste ink pads.
  * *Remediation: 3-Stage Chemical Recovery Protocol:*
    1. *Direct Reverse-Pressure Purging:* Injecting heated surfactant solvent through manifold inlet posts using micro-syringes.
    2. *Ultrasonic Immersion Cavitation:* Submerging head nozzle plate in ultrasonic bath where micro-bubbles implode against hardened external residue.
    3. *Damper Degassing & Priming:* Purging trapped air cushions and restoring continuous hydrodynamic siphon pressure.

### C. Monochrome Laser & Multifunction Printing
* **Mechanics:** Semiconductor laser beam draws latent electrostatic image on photosensitive organic photoconductor (OPC) drum; toner transferred to paper and permanently fused via heat (180°C–200°C) and pressure.
* **Failure Mode: Vertical Black Lines & Toner Smearing:**
  * *Root Cause:* Scratched OPC drum blade or torn Teflon fuser sleeve allowing loose carbon toner to bake onto the heated ceramic element.
  * *Remediation:* Replacement of fuser film sleeve, pressure roller bushing renewal, high-temperature lubrication, and transfer roller cleaning.

### D. Banking Teller Passbook Printers
* **Mechanics:** Specialized auto-alignment document throat printers capable of handling booklets with sewn center seams and variable thickness up to 2.8mm.
* **Failure Mode: Center Seam Pin Breakage & Optical Rejection:**
  * *Root Cause:* High-speed head impact when crossing raised thread spine without automatic platen gap (APG) compensation, coupled with cellulose paper dust blinding optical skew phototransistors.
  * *Remediation:* Feeler-gauge APG calibration, non-static optical sensor air cleansing, and magnetic stripe read/write coil demagnetization.
